chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruvanaikka (திருவானைக்கா), the elephant forest by the Kaveri: the poet confesses bondage to courtesans who sell love by the measure of wealth, the body as a hut of filth, his faults and his trade of begging patrons, rejects the breath-holding yogi who would make the body last, and asks for the feet, Siva-knowledge beyond the stages of practice, and service; the praise names Ganesa, Uma as Akhilandeswari, the Ramayana, the spider and the jambu tree of the shrine, and Murugan as the Tamil child who won at Madurai.
structure_note: Courtesan and desire songs (353, 354, 356, 357, 360, 361, 364, 366); the body and the poet's faults (362, 365, 367); songs of doctrine (355 against the false yogi, 359 on the Absolute beyond chariyai and kiriyai); the poet's confession of begging patrons (358); and a short song for a wise life (363). Song 367 names Arunai, not Thiruvanaikka.

353.reading: The poet lists the arts of women who call with kohl-dark eyes, smile to melt, loosen their hair, show nail-marks on their palms, kindle the fire of desire in young men, bind them with idle talk, bewilder them by dancing in the hall, and take their wealth without blame, and asks whether a day will come when, the bond at these clever hands cut, Murugan grants service at his feet. The praise is first a hymn to Ganesa, elephant-faced, with goad and noose, one tusk and great belly, who cuts the deeds of those who bow, and then names Murugan his younger brother, the six-faced lord of the six syllables who cherished the three Tamils, at the elephant forest by the Jambu tank.
353.nuance: எவரேனும் நிந்தை செய்யாது பொருட்பறிக்கவும்: the courtesans rob without anyone blaming them. The remedy is சேவை, service at the feet. The long praise of Ganesa (விக்கிநப்ரபு, கணராஜன், எங்கள் விநாயகன்) is unusual. கஜாரணியம் and சம்பு தடாகம் name Thiruvanaikka; சுந்தர மாறன் மதில் appears to be a wall built by a Pandya king.

354.reading: The poet asks whether, without singing on his tongue with love and without worshipping the feet with flowers in his hand, he, a wretched sinner, must perish, dimmed in the deceptive charm of women with heavy breasts, bee-hovering hair and blue looks that reach both ears. The praise is a string of names of Uma, the blue tender one, Kundali, Abhirami, Sankari, Parvati of the Veda, and names Murugan her son who embraced the hunter girl, at Thiruvanaikka where Tamil poets and panars sing to the yazh.
354.nuance: The plea defines the loss by what is left undone: பாதமும் அங்கையின் நானில் பூசையும் அணியாமல், the worship of the feet with flowers. ஆலப்போசனி, she who ate the poison, gives Uma Siva's deed.

355.reading: The poet asks not to become a foolish yogi of desire and illusion who, thinking this impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath so it does not leave the nostrils and withers in austerity eating herbs; he asks instead that, with malam, maya and their adjuncts removed, devoted to the conduct of knowledge, knowing 'I am other, my body is other, the whole world is other', he be ruled as a yogi of Siva's own form beyond the mind. The praise names Gopala of the thousand names who plays the flute as uncle, Murugan of Vayalur, and the grove-circled Kavai watered by the Kaveri's flood, which all world-rulers revere.
355.nuance: அனித்தமான ஊன் நாளும் இருப்பதாகவே ... அசட்டு யோகி: the target is breath-holding and herbs used to keep the body, not yoga itself, since the plea ends asking to be a சிவச்சொரூப மாயோகி. யான் வேறு என் உடல் வேறு செகத்து யாவும் வேறாக: release is described as disidentification from body and world.

356.reading: The poet speaks of women whose breasts, smeared with camphor and sandal, burst their bands and make men wither and even ascetics ride the palmyra horse of desire, with carp-like eyes reaching to the ears, and asks whether, on the day Death comes seeking to throw down his body, he will call on Murugan without forgetting his feet. The praise names Murugan on the dark-plumed peacock, the little one younger than the elephant with flowing musth, plunderer of Sura's city, guardian of the gods, servant of the peacock-girl of the millet field, the light of the Tamil Veda, at Kavai.
356.nuance: துறவோரை ஆசை மடல் ஊர்வித்து: the classical madal, the spurned lover's ride on the palmyra horse, is forced even on renouncers. காலைமறவாமல்: the feet are what must be remembered at Death's hour. Some lines of the praise (பாய்மத கபோலத்தானொடு இகலாம் முற்பாடி) are hard to divide.

357.reading: The poet says that, infatuated with women of poison eyes skilled in Kama's arts, who act out desire exactly as far as the money goes even if a thousand measures of gold are paid for their breasts, he suffered weakness, trembling and madness as fate wrote on his head, and asks grace for himself who has built a house that is a worm-filled cave of filth. The praise shows the battle with the giants, ghouls clapping and vultures dancing, says that Murugan gives whatever those who tell of his vel desire, and names him the son of the three-eyed Siva of the white jambu where seven-note Tamil found its fruit.
357.nuance: ஆசை அப்பொருள் ஒக்க நடிப்பவர்: the desire is acted in proportion to the payment. தலையிட்ட விதிப்படி: the poet lays his ruin on the fate written on his head, a rare appeal to fate in these confessions. புழுக்கொள் மலக் குகை வீடு: the body as a house of filth. வெண்ணாவல், the white jambu, is the tree of Thiruvanaikka.

358.reading: The poet voices the begging poet's speech to a patron, 'I am first in the rules of prosody; shall I sing you a madal or a kovai? Fetch palm leaf and stylus; I have seen no one your equal on earth; bring this king of poets gold in a bundle, jewels and gems', and asks whether he must wither in the trouble of such talk. The praise names Murugan who at Tamil Madurai, against those who wear no waist-cloth, put the palm leaf into fire and water and won the name of father of dharma, and the light of the shrine on the Kaveri bank where the spider meditating on Siva wove a canopy.
358.nuance: The confession is of the court poet's begging flattery, quoted in his own voice, including the genres he offers (மடல், கோவை). அரைக்காடை சுற்றார் are the naked Jains, and the leaf put into fire and water (அனற்கே புனற்கே வரைந்த ஏடு) is Sambandar's contest at Madurai: Murugan is identified with Sambandar. சிலந்தி நூல்செய் திருக்காவணம் is the Thiruvanaikka story of the spider that sheltered the linga.

359.reading: The poet describes the One the Vedas proclaim, the supreme light in the upper space, beyond those who practise chariyai and kiriyai, beyond turiya, formless knowledge mingled with world, flesh and life, seen by those with Siva-knowledge, full without lack, without caste or clan, the space the devotees speak of, the true house and sea of bliss, and asks whether, the senses' torment ended, he will gain the feet. The praise names Murugan as the child Guha who removed Indra's sorrow, and the son of the Mother, first of the world, daughter of the Himalaya, Gauri, Kundali, the form of nada, spouse of the lord of the white jambu.
359.nuance: சரியை க்ரியையும் புணர்ந்தவர் எவராலும் ஓத அரிய: the rites of the first two stages cannot reach it, and துரியம் கடந்தது puts it beyond the fourth state. சாதி குலமும் இலது: it has no caste or clan, a pointed phrase. The goddess's names close the song at Thiruvanaikka, where she is Akhilandeswari.

360.reading: The poet calls the women of cloud-dark hair and moon faces thieves of love, total cheats, who take the lives of lustful men ignorant of the higher path, who make arrows their eyes and sing for greed of wealth, and asks grace for himself who perishes by them. The praise names Murugan the bridegroom of the hunter girl, the vel that pierced the two hills while the sea cried out, and the peacock rider whose valour Siva, whose head and feet Vishnu on the serpent bed could not find, admires, at Thiruvanaikka.
360.nuance: பரநெறி உணரா அக்காமுகர் உயிர்பலி கொளும்: the women take the lustful as a sacrifice, and their victims are those who do not know the higher path. The search for Siva's head and feet is given to Vishnu alone here.

361.reading: The poet speaks of women's poison-blue eyes and illusory bodies, and of lust, anger, greed and pride that are not destroyed in him, and asks whether Murugan will not think to rule him at his anklet feet, so that from now on he may love the path of knowledge that the masters of breath praise, and yoga, japa and tapas. The praise has the cock crying 'long live', the peacock dancing and ghoul armies playing in the sky, the vel that ended Sura, Murugan of Vayalur, and Thiruvanaikka where women sing and dance.
361.nuance: காமக் ரோத லோப ... இவை சிதையாத பாவி: the inner enemies are named, though the fourth word is garbled. Unlike 355, here breath practice (வாயு வலம் வரல்) and yoga are part of what the poet hopes for. The division of lines 9 to 11 is uncertain.

362.reading: The poet describes the body as a hut packed with blood, flesh, bone, sinew, worms, bile, phlegm, gut, fat, hair and brain, in which the five senses run into the forest and drive him to the five great sins, so that he never tries the Vedas, Puranas, Agamas, chariyai, kiriyai, worship or meditation; he asks that this fault be removed so he may see the house of bliss. The praise names the single vel that broke Krauncha, the giants, the mango and the sea, Murugan the nephew of Ranganatha of Srirangam whom Brahmins of the six limbs praise as Hari and Govinda, and the son of Sambhunatha of the elephant forest.
362.nuance: The inventory of the body (குருதி புலால் என்பு தோல் நரம்புகள் கிருமிகள் ...) is the same device as the Naladiyar's, but here it explains why the poet's senses ran wild, not why a woman should not be desired. சீரங்கராசன் names Srirangam, across the river from Thiruvanaikka.

363.reading: A very short song: the poet asks whether he must wander apart from those who seek and worship Murugan, and asks to be given the wise life of Madurai of mansions. The praise names him the lover of songs, gracious as milk and honey, sweet to the dancing peacock, at Thiruvanaikka.
363.nuance: மாடக் கூடற் பதி ஞான வாழ்வு may point to the Sambandar episode at Madurai, as in 358, or simply mean wisdom at that city. நானத்தாக is hard to divide.

364.reading: The poet compares a woman's lips to honey, her eyes to poison, her breasts to Meru, her waist to empty space, and describes lovemaking in which his life wanes and his clothes slip, then asks whether he must roam like a clown's monkey for women who give an illusory life, and when he will reach the stilling of mind. The praise retells the Ramayana at length: Rama's message to the forgetful Sugriva that the arrow that killed Vali is not spent, the bridge across the sea and Ravana's fortress broken, and names Murugan the brother-in-law of Kama, Narayana's son.
364.nuance: குரங்கை ஒத்து உழல்வேனோ: the poet sees himself as a performing monkey; the image leads, perhaps by design, into the monkey-king of the praise. மனோலயம் என்று சேர்வேன்: the goal named is the dissolution of mind. The speech to Sugriva is hard to divide, and ஜநமுத in line 3 may stand for ஜலமுத, cloud.

365.reading: The poet heaps names on himself: the wretch proud of running errands at fragrant-haired women's feet, trickster, fool, boaster, worthless, unlearned, all anger, stupid, a sinner of unchanging deeds whose speech fails, fallen into hell, and asks whether a day will come when Murugan asks after him and rules him kindly. The praise is of Uma as Narayani who held the mountain bow to burn the cities, the girl of Kanchi, mother of the sea-girt world, Akhilanda Nayaki of the elephant forest, and names Murugan the nephew of Vishnu who twisted off Ravana's heads.
365.nuance: வினவி முன் அருள்செய்து பாங்கின் ஆள்வது: the hope is that the Lord will take the first step and inquire. The praise gives the burning of the three cities to Uma (மலைசிலை ஒருகையில் வாங்கு நாரணி), and names her as the goddess of both Kanchi and Thiruvanaikka (அகிலாண்ட நாயகி).

366.reading: The poet lists courtesan epithets, women who bewilder with spear eyes, breed lust and anger, roam the streets, send their breasts into battle, speak like cuckoos, drive out men without money, paint their skin and call anyone to bed, plunderers, and asks whether he will escape the net of sorrow. The praise names Rama, the sea of compassion who killed Tataka to guard the sacrifice of sages who bathe at dawn and offer to the sun and recite the Gayatri, as uncle, Murugan of the cane and paddy fields of Vayalur, and the beloved of the Father at Thiruvanaikka.
366.nuance: காசற்றாரை இதத்தில் ஒழிச்சிகள்: the women gently put out those without money. காம க்ரோதம் விளைத்திடு: they breed anger as well as lust. The praise sets Vedic morning rites (தர்ப்பணம், காயத்ரீ செபம்) beside the confession.

367.reading: The poet calls himself cruel, wretched and foolish, one who never melts crying 'Kumara, Guru, Saravanabhava, Muruga, refuge', who falls into the pit of beautiful women who give embraces in measure with wealth, and vows that he will not forget, waking or dreaming, the lotus feet with anklets which once at Arunai came with the compassionate devotees and the Vedas at their side to rule him. The praise names Vishnu who churned the sea with Vasuki and Meru so the gods' hunger ended, the dwarf who measured the worlds, as uncle, and Murugan who, in prattling speech, taught Siva that the meaning is to know the knower.
367.nuance: அருணையில் ஒருவிசை ... வரும் இருபரிபுர கமல மலரடி: the feet came once at Arunai (Tiruvannamalai), apparently the poet's own experience of grace, so the vow rests on memory. அறிவை அறிவது பொருளென அருளிய: the teaching to Siva is given as 'know that which knows', without Om. The courtesans who give union by the measure of wealth (பொருளளவளவு) appear again.

links.note: Tirumular, by Nandi's command, promises that breath tied fast keeps the body for thousands of years; 355 calls the yogi who holds the breath to make the impermanent flesh last a fool. The conflict holds if 722 is read as bodily longevity sought for its own sake and 355 as rejecting that practice, not only its misuse.
Both say the courtesan desires the wealth and not the man; 357 sharpens it into a measure, the desire acted exactly as far as the gold goes.
Both confess the poet's trade of praising unworthy patrons for gold: 352 tells it in summary, 358 quotes the begging speech itself, the boast of prosody and the call for jewels.
Both take the body apart into entrails, fat, blood, bone, sinew and skin. The Naladiyar asks which part is the desired woman; 362 makes the inventory the hut in which the poet's own senses run wild.
Both speak of the Absolute by what cannot reach it: 347 by learning, the mind, the tattvas and the Vedas, 359 by chariyai, kiriyai and the turiya state.

The Kural warns that the sweet words (இன்சொல்) of bangled women who want wealth, not love, bring harm. Among the courtesans' arts 353 lists binding men with idle talk (வம்புரை கூறி வளைத்து இணக்கவும்) and taking their wealth without anyone blaming them (நிந்தை செய்யாது பொருட்பறிக்கவும்). The song shows the Kural's point at work: the talk is the tool and the wealth is the aim, and the harm goes unblamed.

The Kural says a head that does not bow at the feet of the Lord is as useless as a sense organ that cannot sense (கோளில் பொறியின் குணமிலவே). 354 asks whether he must perish without having sung with love on his tongue (அன்புடன் நாவிற் பா) and without worship of the feet by his hand (பாதமும் அங்கையின் நானிற் பூசையும் அணியாமல்). Both measure the bodily organs by whether they serve the feet: the Kural names the head, the song the tongue and the hand.

In the Kural the lover says he once had shame and manliness, and now has only the palmyra horse that the lustful ride (காமுற்றார் ஏறும் மடல்). 356 says the breasts of these women make even renouncers ride the madal of desire (துறவோரை ஆசைமடல் ஊர்வித்து ஆளும்). The song carries the Kural's figure past the lover to the ascetic: the madal now marks the fall of a renouncer, not only of a man's pride.

The Tirumanthiram calls dull (ஊமர்) those who disregard the body as filth (மலமென்று உடம்பை மதியாத), and says that holding it as good grasps the cosmos in it. 357 calls his own body a worm-filled cave of filth he has built as a house (புழுக்கொள் மலக் குகை வீடு கட்டி இருக்கும் எனக்கு). On the reading that மலம் in the Tirumanthiram means filth, the song takes exactly the stance the Tirumanthiram rejects.

The Tirumanthiram places the jnani and the silent one above those of chariyai and kiriyai (தானிக் குலத்தோர் சரியை கிரியையே). 359 describes the One that those who practise chariyai and kiriyai cannot tell (ஓது சரியை க்ரியையும் புணர்ந்தவர் எவராலும் ஓத அரிய), beyond turiya, seen only by those with Siva-knowledge (சிவஞானம் சால உடையவர் கண்டுகொண்டது). Both rank the first two stages below knowledge; the song states it from the side of the goal, the Tirumanthiram from the side of the seeker.

The Tirumanthiram teaches that kin is one and God is one (ஒன்றே குலமும் ஒருவனே தேவனும்). Among the marks of the Absolute, 359 says it has neither caste nor clan (சாதி குலமும் இலது). The Tirumanthiram makes one clan of all people under one God; the song carries the same denial of division into the nature of God itself.

The Kural says the embrace of deceiving women (மாய மகளிர் முயக்கு) is a deadly அணங்கு to those who lack discerning knowledge (ஆயும் அறிவினர் அல்லார்க்கு). 360 says the courtesans take as a sacrifice the lives of the lustful who do not know the higher path (பரநெறி உணரா அக்காமுகர் உயிர்பலி கொளும்). Both find the danger in the man's want of knowledge, and both make it a matter of life and death.

The Tirumanthiram's speaker, having driven off lust, anger and delusion (காமம் வெகுளி மயக்கம் இவைகடிந்து), reaches the abode within the sound Om. 361 calls himself the sinner in whom lust, anger and greed are not destroyed (காமக் க்ரோத லோப ... இவை சிதையாத பாவி) and asks for the path of knowledge, yoga, japa and tapas. The two verses stand on either side of the same condition: the Tirumanthiram speaks after the inner enemies are driven off, the song before, asking for the means.

355, in the same chapter, refuses to be a foolish yogi who holds the breath so it does not leave the nostrils (நாசி அடைதல் அந வாயு ஓடாத வகை சாதித்து) thinking the flesh will last. 361 asks to love the path of knowledge praised by those who make the breath circle (வாயு வலம்வர லாலிப்பார்கள்), and yoga, japa and tapas. Read together, 355 does not reject breath practice as such but its use to keep the impermanent body (அனித்தமான ஊன் நாளும் இருப்பதாகவே).

The Tirumanthiram says five elephants live in the forest (அஞ்சுள ஆனை அடவியுள் வாழ்வன) and the five letters are their goad. 362 says the five senses run into the forest (ஐம்புல அடவியில் ஓடும்) and drive him to the five great sins, so that he never tries worship or meditation. Both place the five senses in a forest; the Tirumanthiram supplies the goad whose absence the song confesses.

358 names Murugan who at Tamil Madurai put the palm leaf into fire and water against the Jains (அனற்கே புனற்கே வரைந்த ஏடு) and won the name of father of dharma. 363 asks to be given the wise life of Madurai of mansions (மாடக் கூடற் பதி ஞான வாழ்வை). Read beside 358, the short song's 'wisdom at Madurai' may point to that same contest of Sambandar, whom the songs identify with Murugan.

The Naladiyar says that even if he were Mal whom the gods worship, women tender as young shoots would send away a man with nothing in his hand, bowing with folded hands (விடுப்பர் தங்கையால் தொழுது). Among the courtesans' traits 366 lists that they gently put out those without money (காசற்றாரை இதத்தில் ஒழிச்சிகள்). Both stress that the dismissal is courteous: the politeness is part of the trade.

The Tirumanthiram says that after knowing the knowledge that knows 'this' (ஈதென்று அறியும் அறிவை அறிந்தபின்) one is of the nature that knows. 367 says Murugan, in prattling speech, taught Siva that the meaning is to know the knower (அறிவை அறிவது பொருளென அருளிய). The song gives as the content of the child's teaching to Siva the same knowing of knowledge that the Tirumanthiram names as the final state.

source_issues: Song 356: one corrupt character in மடலு஡ர்வித் (line 3), probably மடலூர்வித்.
Song 358: one corrupt character in பொற்று஡செடுப்பா (line 7), probably பொற்றூசெடுப்பாய்.
Song 359: one corrupt character in வயலு஡ரா (line 18), probably வயலூரா.
Song 364: one corrupt character in தேனு஡றல் (line 1), probably தேனூறல்; also ஜநமுத (line 3), perhaps for ஜலமுத.
Song 366: one corrupt character in காயத்஡ணசெப (line 15), probably காயத்ரீ செப (஡ண for ரீ).
Song 361: line 6 (காமக் ரோத லோப மப மிவை) seems garbled; the fourth vice is perhaps மதம்.
Song 367 is grouped under திருவானைக்கா but names only Arunai (அருணை) and ends without a shrine.
